currentCapabilities: Action Proposal, Draft, Approval, ExecutionLease, append-only Receipt and reconcile authorities exist
maker, approver and executor separation, expiry, idempotency, tenant isolation, kill and count-based guardrails are tested
AIP CapabilityRevision and tenant-scoped CapabilityBinding authorities exist separately
R4 execution is disabled by the generic Action execution service

findings.finding: Action proposals read mutable meta_action_type rows and derive a snapshot hash; there is no published, install-locked ActionTypeRevision authority or lifecycle used by the Action chain.
server risk is classified by keyword matching over action names, object names and payload keys; it is not resolved from a signed exact risk policy and can misclassify aliases or novel fields.

ActionProposal and ExecutionLease do not bind an exact CapabilityRevision or CapabilityBinding, so catalog readiness, health, quota, network policy and adapter revision are not revalidated before execution.
the proposal, preview and lease contain no exact accountRef; ActionAdapter.execute receives only payload and idempotency key, allowing no authority-level proof of which tenant account will be used.
no production registration of ACTION_ADAPTERS was found; all discovered registrations are test-only, so every real execution currently fails closed with adapter unavailable.

the generic service accepts any existing meta_action_type for proposal creation and permits R2/R3 execution after generic approval; W5 requires an explicit low-risk allowlist while refund, price, inventory, payment and compensation remain independently disabled.

guardrails count one budget unit when a lease is acquired, but do not bind currency, estimated or maximum cost, account budget, reservation, release, measured UsageReceipt or an exact BudgetPolicyRevision.
Action uses R0-R4 while CapabilityRevision uses low, medium, high and critical; no canonical monotonic mapping or conflict rule is implemented.
the guardrail table is enforced at lease time but no versioned CAS command, immutable change receipt, approval policy or installation-overlay binding was found for maintaining it.
the ActionAdapter protocol exposes execute and reconcile only; there is no canonical dryValidate contract for account, permissions, limits, reversibility and provider readiness before approval.

verification.interpretation: the existing generic safety chain is stable, but it is not an operationally authorized ecommerce Action matrix

matrixRules: the effective risk is the maximum of ActionType, Capability, account, batch size, data marking, reversibility and policy floors; aliases can never lower it
every executable row must bind exact ActionTypeRevision, CapabilityRevision, CapabilityBinding, accountRef, AdapterRevision, BudgetPolicyRevision and kill policy
read and draft-only capabilities do not become external Actions merely because the UI exposes a button
unknown readiness, health, cost, account, policy or provider outcome is blocked; it cannot fall back to another account or adapter
R4 and all unlisted ActionTypes remain disabled; each R2 or R3 row requires its own explicit specialized policy and canary authorization
Secret values never enter the matrix, proposal, preview, receipt, logs or shared memory; only opaque refs are allowed
